reason: The cited evidence (E3, E4) directly supports the formation of isolated active sites, charge-transfer, and enhanced adsorption/activity for PtPdCoCuNi HEA in nitrobenzene hydrogenation, but the general claim of tunable synergy across compositions and the comparison to conventional catalysts are only partially supported by the specific HEA systems studied in E1 and E2, which focus on different reactions and do not explicitly demonstrate a generalizable synergy mechanism.
premises: Multiple active sites in HEAs can be tuned by varying composition and structure
Synergy between multiple active sites enhances adsorption of reactants and intermediates
Isolated active sites form in HEAs and enable charge-transfer between sites
Charge-transfer to active sites enhances catalytic activity
HEA catalysts with optimized composition/structure outperform conventional single-active-site catalysts
